result.title: Unlocking Structured Pruning for Reasoning Language Models via Attention-Preserving MLP Trimming
result.summary: Structured pruning reduces LLM inference costs by removing model components to produce smaller dense models. However, existing methods can cause reasoning performance to collapse on long-form reasoning tasks such as AIME. We propose \textit{LayerTrim}, a training-free structured pruning method that identifies redundant decoder layers and selectively trims their MLP features while preserving attention and decoder depth. LayerTrim is the first training-free structured pruning method designed to preserve long-form reasoning without gradients or recovery training. Across three reasoning language models and five benchmarks, LayerTrim outperforms existing structured pruning methods in most evaluated settings, improving average accuracy by up to 21.4 percentage points over RESP. On \texttt{Qwen3-14B}, LayerTrim achieves 1.24$\times$ faster prefill and 19.7\% lower peak GPU memory than the dense model, while better preserving reasoning ability. It also achieves the shortest average generation length among evaluated pruned models, while retaining the highest average accuracy. These results demonstrate that LayerTrim improves reasoning efficiency through both structural compression and reduced token generation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LayerTrim，一种免训练的结构化剪枝方法：识别冗余解码层并只裁剪其 MLP 特征，保留注意力与层深，以维持长链条推理能力，在多个推理模型与基准上兼顾精度与推理解码效率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「保留注意力、裁剪 MLP」的经验结论可能提示推理相关计算更依赖注意力路径，且其压缩后生成长度缩短的观察与长推理成本问题相关，可供核查；但论文不涉及 latent 状态生成或多模态视觉证据，与 LVR 主线仅有间接线索。
